aegisVigilBridge.text: RFV Aegis Vigil bridge — broad heavy-cruiser command space organized around protection and convoy awareness. A central command position faces a large shared tactical-and-route display; navigation, communications, escort control and damage status stations form a functional arc. Civilian contacts, distress calls and protected assets remain visible alongside threats. Deep Fleet blue, Ion White working surfaces, restrained gold details, and signs of long maintenance rather than showroom polish.

aegisVigilRescueControl.text: Aegis Vigil rescue-control room — compact operations center adjacent to hangar and docking systems, with live compartment maps, pressure diagrams, docking-collar status, rescue-team boards, medical intake counts, shuttle assignments and civilian manifests. Built for several simultaneous incidents rather than ceremonial command.

aegisVigilEngineering.text: Aegis Vigil engineering — dense, heavily redundant machinery spaces with accessible service trunks, isolation valves, power buses, coolant lines, pressure doors, repair lockers and damage-control routes. Systems show layers of replacement and careful maintenance; critical load paths should be visually understandable when they fail.

aegisVigilMedical.text: Aegis Vigil medical complex — permanent treatment rooms backed by modular overflow capacity that can expand into adjacent bays. Clear triage markings, practical equipment, secured supplies, decontamination points and movable treatment stations support both crew medicine and civilian mass-casualty intake.

aegisVigilHangar.text: Aegis Vigil hangar and boat deck — rescue cutters, shuttles, utility craft, tow gear, pressure shelters, cargo movers and modular relief pallets dominate the deck. The space can support combat craft but is visually defined by launch, retrieval, transfer and repair work.

aegisVigilDockingSpine.text: Aegis Vigil docking spine — reinforced transfer corridor linking multiple docking collars, emergency pressure sections and cargo interfaces. Designed to receive damaged civilian craft and move people, supplies and equipment without routing everything through one choke point.

aegisVigilMess.text: Aegis Vigil mess and common deck — durable crew space with bolted tables, hot-food service, duty boards, worn seating and the small personal marks of people who spend long escort cycles aboard. It should feel inhabited and functional, not military-theatrical.

bastionSpireAegisBerth.text: Bastion Spire Aegis berth — heavy-cruiser mooring and relief-loading complex with fuel umbilicals, repair gantries, cargo lifts, public-facing aid staging and Aegis Crown heraldry used as factional tradition rather than ship naming. Aegis Vigil's hull should visibly dwarf service craft without becoming architecturally abstract.

civilianConvoyInterior.text: Civilian convoy vessel interior — working transport space whose design follows purpose rather than Fleet standardization: cargo restraints, passenger bunks, agricultural modules, tool lockers, patched systems and locally maintained controls. Preserve the vessel's specific function whenever used.

corridorRescueZone.text: Corridor rescue zone — navigable space around a disabled ship, unstable route boundary, debris field or failing beacon line. Approach vectors, hazards, rescue craft and the path back to safety must remain physically readable.

aegisVigilExterior.text: RFV Aegis Vigil exterior — large Rex Fleet heavy cruiser built for escort endurance and rescue access rather than ornamental menace: a long armored central hull, broad protected machinery shoulders, visible docking and boat-deck apertures, layered point-defense coverage, multiple service hardpoints and a weathered blue-white-gold Fleet finish. The silhouette should communicate mass, redundancy and the ability to put itself between danger and smaller ships.

wayfarerNineBridge.text: Wayfarer Nine bridge — compact Verge civilian convoy-control space with worn manual controls, route boards, cargo-temperature panels, patched seats and a wide forward view of neighboring ships. Green practical markings identify civilian route responsibility without making the vessel look Fleet-standard.

goodMeasureInterior.text: Good Measure interior — aging Verge freight vessel with narrow pressure corridors, exposed service panels, patched insulation, agricultural cold-storage trunks and machinery repaired across decades by different hands. Damage should propagate through understandable physical systems: pressure doors, coolant loops, power trunks and docking hardware.

fieldglassCargoDeck.text: Fieldglass cargo deck — working agricultural carrier packed with secured produce modules, replacement machinery, water-system parts and heavy freight pallets. During emergency mass reduction, crews physically release selected cargo through marked handling lanes; the loss should look economically painful rather than spectacular.
